newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal's 1997 growth may exceed 6 pct - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Senegal's 1997 growth may exceed 6 pct - IMF.

text.p: Senegal's economy could grow by more than six percent in 1997, Samba Thiam, the International Monetary Fund's representative in the country, told a news conference on Tuesday.
That compares with a growth rate of 5.2 percent in 1996 and 4.8 percent in 1995.
"We believe that Senegal is on the right track for sustained, durable growth," Thiam said.

"The growth rate, particularly in the non-agricultural sector, could be close to six percent, or even higher, for the current year. I should also note that since 1995 the growth rate of the economy has far exceeded the demographic growth rate."
Inflation, as measured by the consumer price index, rose by three percent in 1996, well down from 8.1 percent in 1995.
"And in the first few months of 1997, with the exception of one month, inflation has been negative," Thiam said.
The government's aim is to cut the inflation rate to 2.5 percent in 1997.

The budget deficit was equivalent to two percent of gross domestic product in 1996, down from 3.2 percent in 1995, and for the first time the primary budget account, excluding debt service charges, was in surplus.
"That means that Senegal is on the road to financial viability, on condition that its efforts in the field of revenue recovery are reinforced," Thiam said.
